big_ideas.title: Energy is conserved
big_ideas.text: Every problem starts as an energy balance on a control volume or a surface — in, out, generated, stored. The balance, not a memorised formula, is what fixes the answer.

big_ideas.title: Rates follow driving potential over resistance
big_ideas.text: Conduction, convection and radiation each move heat at a rate set by a temperature difference and a resistance; resistances add in series and parallel, and the largest one controls.

big_ideas.title: Temperature is a field set by an equation and its boundaries
big_ideas.text: The heat equation plus boundary and initial conditions determines T everywhere; geometry and boundaries, not the material alone, shape the profile.

big_ideas.title: Dimensionless groups decide the model
big_ideas.text: Bi, Fo, Re, Pr, Gr, Ra and Nu say which simplification is valid — lumped or not, laminar or turbulent, free or forced — before any number is computed.

big_ideas.title: Real systems are networks of modes
big_ideas.text: Devices combine conduction, convection and radiation in series and parallel; analysing and designing them means building that network and finding the bottleneck.

practices.title: Define the system
practices.text: Draw the control volume or surface, label every energy term (in, out, generation, storage), state steady or transient.

practices.title: Set up the model
practices.text: State the assumptions (1-D, constant k, …) and translate the physical description into the governing equation and boundary/initial conditions.

practices.title: Choose the right relation
practices.text: Pick the correlation, shape factor, chart or solution that fits — check its validity range (Re, Ra, Pr, Bi, geometry) and the temperature properties are evaluated at.

practices.title: Compute with units
practices.text: SI throughout, kelvin for radiation and property tables, per-unit-length vs per-area vs total rates kept straight.

practices.title: Check the answer
practices.text: Signs and directions, limiting cases, orders of magnitude (typical h, k), energy closes.

practices.title: Reason and design
practices.text: Sketch profiles, predict what changes when a parameter changes, compare options, size a design to a constraint.

topics.title: The three modes and their rate equations

los.do: Identify which modes act in a described system and write the rate law for each.
ek: Conduction needs a medium; convection needs fluid motion; radiation needs neither.

los.do: Calculate a conduction flux or rate, or an unknown k, from Fourier's law across a plane layer.
ek: q'' = k ΔT / L; heat flows down the temperature gradient.

los.do: Calculate a convection rate from Newton's law of cooling and judge whether h is plausible.
ek: q = hA(T_s − T∞); h ~ 2–25 free gas, 25–250 forced gas, 50–20 000 forced liquid, 2 500–100 000 phase change (W/m²·K).

los.do: Calculate net radiation between a small surface and large surroundings, and linearise it to a radiation coefficient h_r.
ek: q'' = εσ(T_s⁴ − T_sur⁴) in kelvin; h_r = εσ(T_s + T_sur)(T_s² + T_sur²).

topics.title: Energy balances on control volumes and surfaces

los.do: Apply conservation of energy to a control volume: in − out + generated = stored.
ek: Generation is volumetric (I²R, reaction); storage is ρcV dT/dt; both vanish from a surface balance.

los.do: Apply a surface energy balance linking conduction, convection and radiation at a boundary.
ek: A surface has no volume: what conducts in, convects and radiates out.

los.do: Find the instantaneous rate of temperature change of a body from an unsteady energy balance.
ek: dT/dt = (Σq_in − Σq_out + Ė_g)/(ρcV) at that instant.

units.title: The heat equation and boundary conditions

los.do: Calculate heat flux (magnitude and direction) from a given temperature field.
ek: q'' = −k∇T; flux points from hot to cold, normal to isotherms.

los.do: Use k, ρc_p and α = k/ρc_p to compare how materials conduct, store and diffuse heat.
ek: High k moves heat; high ρc_p stores it; α sets how fast a disturbance spreads.

los.do: Write the heat equation in Cartesian, cylindrical or spherical coordinates and simplify it for a stated case (steady, 1-D, no generation, constant k).
ek: (1/r)d/dr(r dT/dr) and (1/r²)d/dr(r² dT/dr) are the radial Laplacians; each assumption strikes a term.

los.do: From a given T field, find the generation rate, the surface fluxes or the local rate of change ∂T/∂t.
ek: k∇²T + q̇ = ρc ∂T/∂t; read each term off the derivatives of T.

los.do: Decide whether a temperature field can be a steady, generation-free solution.
ek: Steady, no q̇, constant k ⇒ ∇²T = 0 (Laplace).

los.do: Translate a physical boundary into its mathematical condition: fixed temperature, fixed flux, insulated or symmetry plane, convection, radiation, perfect-contact interface.
ek: −k dT/dx|_s = q''_s; insulated or symmetric ⇒ dT/dx = 0; convection: −k dT/dx|_s = h(T_s − T∞); interface: T and k dT/dx continuous.

los.do: Write the complete formulation (equation + two BCs, or + IC) of a 1-D problem from a word description.
ek: A second-order ODE needs two independent conditions; a transient one also needs T(x, 0).

los.do: Sketch T(x) and read boundary conditions and k ratios from slopes.
ek: Insulated ⇒ zero slope; in series, slope ∝ 1/k; with generation the profile curves (concave down for q̇ > 0).

topics.title: The plane wall and thermal resistance

los.do: Find T(x) and q in a plane wall with fixed-temperature or convective boundaries.
ek: No generation ⇒ linear T(x); q is the same at every x.

los.do: Build a series–parallel resistance network for a composite wall and compute q, U and every interface temperature.
ek: R_cond = L/kA, R_conv = 1/hA; series add, parallel add as conductances; U = 1/(R_tot A).

los.do: Include thermal contact resistance and judge when it matters.
ek: R''_t,c in series at the interface; matters when it rivals L/k of the layers.

los.do: Reason qualitatively about a network: same q in series, largest ΔT across the largest R, which change helps most.
ek: ΔT_i / ΔT_tot = R_i / R_tot.

los.do: Find q and T(x) when the cross-section A(x) or k(T) varies, by integrating Fourier's law with q constant.
ek: Steady, no q̇ ⇒ q_x constant; q ∫dx/A(x) = −∫k(T)dT.

los.do: Calculate q′ and T(r) for a cylindrical wall or insulated pipe using its resistance.
ek: R′ = ln(r₂/r₁)/(2πk); T(r) is logarithmic.

los.do: Calculate q for a spherical shell using its resistance.
Find the critical insulation radius and decide whether adding insulation raises or lowers q.
ek: r_cr = k/h (cylinder), 2k/h (sphere); below r_cr insulation increases q.

los.do: State which quantities stay constant with radius in steady radial conduction.
ek: q (or q′) is constant; q″ falls as 1/r (cylinder) or 1/r² (sphere).

los.do: Find the surface temperature from an overall energy balance before solving for the profile.
ek: Everything generated leaves through the cooled surfaces: q̇V = hA(T_s − T∞).

los.do: Solve for the parabolic T(x) and T_max with symmetric fixed-temperature or convective boundaries.
ek: T_max − T_s = q̇L²/2k; the midplane (or insulated face) is adiabatic.

los.do: With unequal face temperatures, locate the maximum and find the flux through each face.
ek: x_max = k(T₂ − T₁)/(2q̇L); more heat leaves through the cooler face.

los.do: Analyse a generating layer bonded to non-generating layers, chaining flux, interface and maximum temperatures.
ek: Flux leaving the generating layer = q̇L_A and passes unchanged through the plain layers.

los.do: Find surface and centreline temperatures of a solid cylinder or wire with generation, including q̇ from Joule heating.
ek: T_s = T∞ + q̇r_o/2h; T₀ − T_s = q̇r_o²/4k; q̇ = I²ρ_e/A².

los.do: Find surface and centre temperatures of a sphere with generation.
ek: T_s = T∞ + q̇r_o/3h; T₀ − T_s = q̇r_o²/6k.

los.do: Solve a hollow cylinder with generation and one insulated or convective surface.
ek: General T = −q̇r²/4k + C₁ ln r + C₂; apply one BC per surface.

los.do: Find the largest allowable q̇, or the h or thickness needed, to keep T_max below a limit.
ek: T_max − T∞ = q̇L/h + q̇L²/2k: a film rise plus a conduction rise.

topics.title: The fin equation and its solutions

los.do: Derive the fin equation from an energy balance on a fin element and compute m for a given geometry.
ek: d²θ/dx² − m²θ = 0, m² = hP/kA_c; θ = T − T∞.

los.do: Choose the tip condition (infinite, adiabatic, convective via corrected length) and compute fin heat rate and tip or local temperature.
ek: q_f = M tanh mL (adiabatic); M = √(hPkA_c)θ_b; L_c = L + D/4 for a pin.

los.do: Explain why fin temperature decays exponentially rather than linearly, and how to change the decay.
ek: Side convection removes heat along the length; larger m (low k, high h, thin) ⇒ faster decay.

los.do: Calculate fin efficiency and effectiveness and decide whether a fin is worthwhile.
ek: η_f = q_f/(hA_fθ_b); ε_f = q_f/(hA_c,bθ_b); fins pay off when ε_f ≳ 2, i.e. high k, low h.

los.do: Calculate overall surface efficiency and heat rate of a fin array and its resistance.
ek: η_o = 1 − (NA_f/A_t)(1 − η_f); q_t = η_o h A_t θ_b; R_t,o = 1/(η_o h A_t).

los.do: Set up the separable solution for a rectangle with one non-homogeneous edge and evaluate its leading terms.
ek: θ = Σ C_n sin(nπx/L) sinh(nπy/L)/sinh(nπW/L); homogeneous BCs set the eigenfunctions.

los.do: Pick the matching shape-factor case and compute q = Sk ΔT.
ek: S has units of length; R = 1/Sk; check the geometric validity condition.

los.do: Combine shape-factor resistances with other resistances in a network.
ek: Two buried objects ⇒ two resistances in series across T₁ − T₂.

los.do: Write the finite-difference equation of an interior, surface or corner node by an energy balance on its cell, including Δx ≠ Δy, convection and radiation.
ek: Each face: conductance × (T_neighbour − T_m); boundary faces get h·ℓ or h_r·ℓ terms; half cells on edges.

los.do: Solve a small node system directly or by Gauss–Seidel iteration and check the energy balance.
ek: Iterate T_i = (Σa_jT_j + b)/a_i until changes are below tolerance.

los.do: Compute the Biot number with L_c = V/A_s and decide whether lumped capacitance applies.
ek: Bi = hL_c/k < 0.1 ⇒ internal gradients negligible; L_c = r/3 sphere, r/2 cylinder, half-thickness wall.

los.do: Find temperature at a time, or the time to reach a temperature, for a lumped body.
ek: θ/θ_i = exp(−t/τ), τ = ρVc/hA_s.

los.do: Find the energy transferred over an interval.
ek: Q = ρVcθ_i[1 − exp(−t/τ)].

los.do: Set up and solve a general lumped balance with radiation, surface flux or generation.
ek: ρVc dT/dt = q''_sA − hA(T − T∞) − εσA(T⁴ − T_sur⁴) + Ė_g; solve or integrate numerically.

los.do: Compute Bi and Fo and find the centre temperature of a wall, cylinder or sphere with the one-term approximation.
ek: θ₀* = C₁exp(−ζ₁²Fo), valid for Fo > 0.2; ζ₁, C₁ from Bi (wall uses half-thickness).

los.do: Find the temperature at another position, or the time to reach a temperature.
ek: θ* = θ₀* cos(ζ₁x*) (wall), θ₀* J₀(ζ₁r*) (cylinder), θ₀* sin(ζ₁r*)/(ζ₁r*) (sphere).

los.do: Find the fraction of the maximum energy transferred, Q/Q₀.
ek: Wall: Q/Q₀ = 1 − (sin ζ₁/ζ₁)θ₀*; cylinder and sphere have their own forms.

los.do: Find temperature at a depth and time, the depth reached, or the time needed, after a sudden surface temperature change.
ek: (T − T_s)/(T_i − T_s) = erf(x/2√(αt)); valid while the far side hasn't felt it.

los.do: Find the surface heat flux, and the contact temperature when two semi-infinite solids touch.
ek: q''_s = k(T_s − T_i)/√(παt); T_s = (√(kρc)_A T_A + √(kρc)_B T_B)/(√(kρc)_A + √(kρc)_B).

los.do: Build a 2-D or 3-D transient solution as a product of 1-D solutions.
ek: Short cylinder = infinite cylinder × plane wall, each in dimensionless θ*.

los.do: Write the explicit finite-difference equation for a transient node and check its stability limit.
ek: T_m^{p+1} = Fo(T_{m+1}^p + T_{m−1}^p) + (1 − 2Fo)T_m^p; stable if Fo ≤ 1/2 (interior, 1-D).

los.do: Compute Re, Pr and Nu and identify laminar, transitional or turbulent flow.
ek: Re_x = u∞x/ν (transition ≈ 5×10⁵ on a plate); Pr = ν/α; Nu = hL/k_f.

los.do: Relate local and average convection coefficients.
ek: h̄ = (1/L)∫h_x dx; laminar h_x ∝ x^(−1/2) ⇒ h̄ = 2h_x(L).

los.do: Estimate velocity and thermal boundary-layer thicknesses and how Pr relates them.
Use the Reynolds–Colburn analogy to get h from friction (or friction from h).

topics.title: The flat plate in parallel flow

los.do: Calculate average h and q for laminar flow over a flat plate, with properties at the film temperature.
Calculate average h for a mixed laminar–turbulent boundary layer.

topics.title: Cylinders and spheres in cross flow

los.do: Calculate h and q for a cylinder or sphere in cross flow with the appropriate correlation.
ek: Churchill–Bernstein (cylinder, Re Pr > 0.2); Whitaker (sphere, μ ratio).

los.do: Find the maximum velocity, average h and outlet temperature for flow across a tube bank.
ek: V_max from the minimum free area (aligned vs staggered); Žukauskas Nu̅ with row correction; log-mean ΔT across the bank.

los.do: Compute Re_D from ṁ and decide whether the flow is laminar and how long the entry regions are.
ek: Re_D = 4ṁ/(πDμ); laminar below ≈ 2300; x_fd,h ≈ 0.05 Re_D D; x_fd,t ≈ 0.05 Re_D Pr D.

los.do: Find outlet temperature or required length with uniform wall heat flux.
ek: q = ṁc_p(T_m,o − T_m,i) = q''_s πDL; T_m rises linearly.

los.do: Find outlet temperature or heat rate with uniform wall temperature, using the log-mean temperature difference.
ek: ΔT_o/ΔT_i = exp(−PL h̄/ṁc_p); q = h̄A_s ΔT_lm.

los.do: Use the fully developed laminar results for constant flux or constant wall temperature.
ek: Nu_D = 4.36 (uniform q''_s), 3.66 (uniform T_s).

los.do: Calculate h for turbulent flow with Dittus–Boelter (or Gnielinski), choosing the right exponent and property temperature.
ek: Nu_D = 0.023 Re^(4/5) Pr^n, n = 0.4 heating, 0.3 cooling; properties at mean T_m.

los.do: Use the hydraulic diameter and annulus results for noncircular passages.
ek: D_h = 4A_c/P; laminar Nu depends on shape; annulus uses D_o − D_i.

topics.title: Buoyancy-driven flow and when it matters

los.do: Compute Gr and Ra and identify laminar or turbulent free convection.
ek: Ra_L = gβΔT L³/(να); β = 1/T_f for an ideal gas; transition near Ra ≈ 10⁹ on a vertical plate.

los.do: Decide whether free, forced or mixed convection governs.
ek: Gr/Re² ≪ 1 forced, ≫ 1 free, ~1 mixed.

los.do: Calculate h for a vertical plate with the Churchill–Chu correlation.
Calculate h for horizontal plates (hot side up or down) and horizontal cylinders and spheres.
ek: L = A_s/P for horizontal plates; separate correlations for upper/lower surfaces.

los.do: Calculate heat transfer across a vertical or horizontal enclosure (e.g. double-pane window).
ek: Ra_L across the gap; Nu = 1 means pure conduction below the critical Ra.

los.do: Use Stefan–Boltzmann and Wien's law to relate emissive power, peak wavelength and temperature.
ek: E_b = σT⁴; λ_max T = 2898 μm·K.

los.do: Find the fraction of blackbody emission in a wavelength band.
ek: F(0→λ) from λT (Table 12.2); band = difference of two fractions.

los.do: Find total emissivity or absorptivity from spectral data and apply Kirchhoff's law and the gray-surface assumption.
ek: α = ∫α_λG_λdλ / G; ε = α only for a gray or diffuse-gray surface at the same T.

los.do: Solve a surface energy balance with irradiation, emission and convection for a steady surface temperature.
ek: αG = εσT⁴ (+ h(T − T∞)) at steady state.

los.do: Find view factors with reciprocity, summation and symmetry, including long ducts and cavities.
ek: A_iF_ij = A_jF_ji; Σ_j F_ij = 1; flat or convex surfaces have F_ii = 0.

los.do: Evaluate view factors for standard geometries from formulas or charts.
ek: Concentric cylinders/spheres: F₁₂ = 1; coaxial disks, aligned rectangles from Tables 13.1–13.2.

los.do: Calculate net exchange between black surfaces.
ek: q_ij = A_iF_ijσ(T_i⁴ − T_j⁴).

los.do: Calculate net exchange in a two-surface gray enclosure (parallel plates, concentric cylinders or spheres).
ek: q = σ(T₁⁴ − T₂⁴)/[(1−ε₁)/ε₁A₁ + 1/A₁F₁₂ + (1−ε₂)/ε₂A₂].

los.do: Quantify the effect of radiation shields.
ek: Each shield adds two surface resistances and one space resistance in series.

los.do: Solve a three-surface enclosure with a reradiating (adiabatic) surface by the radiosity network.
ek: Reradiating: J = E_b at that surface, net q = 0.

los.do: Combine radiation exchange with conduction and convection at a surface or in an enclosure.
ek: Radiation and convection from one surface act in parallel; h_r lets radiation join the resistance network.

units.title: Heat exchangers and system-level thermal analysis

los.do: Calculate U for a tube wall including both films, fouling and finned surfaces.
ek: 1/UA = 1/(η_o hA)_c + R''_f,c/(η_oA)_c + R_w + R''_f,h/(η_oA)_h + 1/(η_o hA)_h.

los.do: Size a parallel-flow or counterflow exchanger with q = UA ΔT_lm when all inlet and outlet temperatures are known.
ek: ΔT_lm = (ΔT₁ − ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂), end differences defined by flow arrangement; counterflow needs less area.

los.do: Apply the LMTD correction factor for shell-and-tube and cross-flow exchangers.
ek: q = UAF ΔT_lm,CF with F from P and R charts.

los.do: Find effectiveness and heat rate from NTU and C_r.
ek: NTU = UA/C_min; C_r = C_min/C_max; ε from the arrangement's relation; q = εC_min(T_h,i − T_c,i).

los.do: Predict outlet temperatures of an existing exchanger when they are unknown.
ek: ε–NTU avoids iteration when outlets are unknown; then energy balances give each outlet.

los.do: Model a device (electronics package, building wall, pipe run) as a network of conduction, convection and radiation resistances and find its operating temperature.
ek: One energy balance per node; parallel paths from a surface (convection ∥ radiation); iterate when h_r depends on T.

los.do: Identify the controlling resistance and choose the design change that best meets a temperature limit.
ek: Reduce the largest R first; compare options by their effect on R_tot.

los.do: Identify the boiling regime from the excess temperature on the boiling curve.
ek: Free convection → nucleate → transition → film; CHF at the nucleate peak.

los.do: Calculate nucleate boiling flux (Rohsenow) and critical heat flux.
ek: q''_s ∝ ΔT_e³; q''_max = 0.149 h_fg ρ_v [σg(ρ_l − ρ_v)/ρ_v²]^(1/4).

los.do: Calculate film condensation on a vertical plate or horizontal tube.
ek: Nusselt analysis with h′_fg = h_fg(1 + 0.68 Ja); tube constant 0.729.

los.do: Calculate a diffusive flux in a stationary medium with Fick's law, including membranes and solubility.
ek: N_A = −D_AB dC_A/dx; at an interface C = S·p.

los.do: Calculate evaporation through a stagnant gas column (Stefan flow).
Solve diffusion with a homogeneous reaction.
ek: D d²C/dx² − k₁C = 0 ⇒ cosh/sinh profile, like a fin.

topics.title: Convective mass transfer and the analogy

los.do: Use the heat–mass analogy to convert between h and h_m, and Nu and Sh correlations.
ek: h/h_m = ρc_p Le^(2/3); Sh = f(Re, Sc) mirrors Nu = f(Re, Pr).

los.do: Solve a coupled heat and mass balance at an evaporating surface (wet bulb).
ek: h(T∞ − T_s) = h_m h_fg(ρ_A,s − ρ_A,∞).
